title.purpose: The top of the ladder; there is no display size.

meta.purpose: The line under a title: keys, timestamps, notes, refusals.

label.purpose: Tile headers, kv keys, column headers, chips: uppercase and tracked.

kbd.purpose: Key hints inside tile headers and buttons.

number.purpose: A number inside a row: text size, never bigger.

stat.purpose: Project outcome tiles only: the one place a number is allowed to be big.

doc-h1.purpose: Design and description headings, step 1 of 6.

doc-h6.purpose: Step 6: a label, uppercase and tracked, mute.

shadows.name: focus-inset
shadows.purpose: The focused tile: with the border switched to --gf-system, the only effect in the system. Every other box-shadow is refused by lint.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Hover, focus, selection, the refusal fade-in. 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: move
motion.purpose: Tiles resizing, rows reordering. 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: breathe
motion.purpose: The one ambient animation: a live run's node, opacity. animation: none under prefers-reduced-motion, never 0s.

breakpoints.name: crumb-hides
breakpoints.purpose: At and below this the crumb leaves the bar; trash and settings never do.

breakpoints.name: bar-collapses
breakpoints.purpose: At and below this the bar shows workspace numbers and counts only.

breakpoints.name: laptop
breakpoints.purpose: The desk becomes a 2-column tile grid.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: 3 columns: more tiles open rather than the same tiles getting bigger.

breakpoints.name: ultrawide
breakpoints.purpose: 4 columns. The kanban spans every column and caps its own columns at 280px.

narrative.overview:
A tracker that is a **control surface and a memory**, not a Linear clone. The visual model is a **tiling window manager**: a status bar with workspaces, tiles with gaps, one focused tile, keyboard hints in every title bar. Flat, matte, square. Colour carries meaning; almost nothing is decorative.

Three references, distilled: Linear's keyboard-first discipline and single-accent restraint; Everforest's warm, low-glare palette; a HUD's honesty about telemetry (numbers you read, not numbers you admire).

Everything on screen is a line in the bar or a tile on the desk. A tile's title bar names it in mono caps, says what its keys do, and takes the system colour on its border when it is the focused one; its body is rows, or cards on the kanban. The density is a working tool's: type runs from 10.5 to 22 pixels and only a project's outcome tiles are allowed a big number. The one confirmed rejection is the magazine. A ticket design is not one, so there is no display type, no hero number and no editorial whitespace anywhere in the GUI.
keyCharacteristics: Everforest dark, matte and opaque: three surface steps and 1px rules do all the work of depth.
Square everywhere; the focused tile's border and inset is the only effect.
One accent, one meaning; red is your attention and nothing else.
IBM Plex Sans for words, JetBrains Mono for anything that is data.
Keyboard first: every tile header shows its keys, and a drag always has a key that does the same thing.
A refusal is one plain sentence, inline, that clears itself.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Each accent has one meaning. A new state first asks whether an existing meaning covers it, and `--gf-human` is your attention and nothing else — removing a dependency brightens to ink rather than inventing a destructive red.

rules.name: The Blocked Is Not A Colour Rule
rules.body: Blocked is a derived condition: an outline glyph and a struck title, never a hue and never opacity.

rules.name: The Text-Safe Rule
rules.body: Every colour that carries words clears 4.5:1 on `--gf-tile`. `--gf-dim` carries no words.

rules.name: The Mono Is A Signal Rule
rules.body: Mono says "this is data, a key, a path". A whole paragraph in mono is a bug, not a mood.

rules.name: The Text-Size Telemetry Rule
rules.body: A number inside a row is text size (Mono 500 15). Only a project outcome tile gets Mono 500 22.

rules.name: The Tile Width Rule
rules.body: The number to hold is the tile width, not the column count: a wider desk opens more tiles rather than stretching the same ones, and the kanban, the one tile that spans the desk, caps its columns at 280px for the same reason.

rules.name: The One Effect Rule
rules.body: Depth is three opaque steps and a 1px rule. The focused tile's `--gf-system` border and 1px inset is the only effect in the system; `bun run lint` refuses any `box-shadow` that is not an inset.

rules.name: The Square Rule
rules.body: `--gf-radius` is `0` and nothing else is allowed on `border-radius`. Browser-native rounding on focus outlines and `<kbd>` is let be.

rules.name: The Inline Refusal Rule
rules.body: A refusal is one mono sentence in `--gf-mute`, placed where the action was refused, clearing on the next click or drag or after 4s. Never a modal, never a toast.

rules.name: The Whole Card Rule
rules.body: The whole card is the drag target: no grip, no handle, no affordance drawn on it.

dos: Do take every colour from a token: `var(--gf-*)`, never a literal. `bun run lint` refuses hex in `web/src`.
Do give a new state an existing meaning before you reach for a new colour, and say what the colour means in the status note or the column header, not only in the hue.
Do set identifiers, keys, paths, timestamps and numbers in JetBrains Mono, and words in IBM Plex Sans.
Do keep a number inside a row at text size (Mono 500 15); only a project outcome tile gets Mono 500 22.
Do write the run cost as `$x.xx / cap`, spent first, cap second, in mute.
Do show every tile's keys in its header, and give every drag a key that does the same thing.
Do refuse with one plain sentence, inline, where the action was refused, and let it clear itself.
Do show blocked as ◇ and a struck title, and cancelled as a struck title in mute.
Do hold the tile width when the desk widens: open more tiles, cap the kanban's columns at 280px.
Do let browser-native focus outlines and `<kbd>` round themselves.
donts: Don't use a `border-radius` other than `0`, a gradient, a shadow that is not the focus inset, a blur, or a glow.
Don't use opacity as a state mark; `.gf-btn:disabled` is the one documented exception, because a disabled control is a missing affordance, not a state.
Don't use `--gf-human` for anything but "your attention is required", and don't invent a destructive red.
Don't use `--gf-live` for "in progress"; orange means a run is alive and costing money, and until a run row exists a hand-built `building` ticket is `--gf-system`.
Don't set a whole paragraph in mono, or put `--gf-dim` on words.
Don't raise a modal or a toast for a refusal, a confirm, or a save state.
Don't add a grip, a handle or an icon to a card; the card is the drag target and marks are glyphs.
Don't reach for stock Everforest values for small text; the palette here was lifted to clear 4.5:1 on `--gf-tile`.
Don't add a marquee, scanline, pulse-glow or spring; the live node's breathe is the one ambient animation.
Don't draw a pie chart, a hero number or display type; a ticket design is not a magazine.
